fieldValues.title: Cloud-agent sandbox has no working SSH commit-signing infrastructure — CLAUDE.md's local-CLI signing instructions cannot be satisfied here
fieldValues.summary: CLAUDE.md's git-signing section says to verify a loaded ssh-agent key (ssh-add -l | grep SHA256:vHuO6...) before committing, and to stop rather than bypass signing if missing. In this session's remote-execution sandbox: ssh-add is not on PATH at all (command not found); git is configured gpg.format=ssh with user.signingkey pointing at /home/claude/.ssh/commit_signing_key.pub, but that file is empty (0 bytes) and no matching private key exists anywhere in the container. A plain `git commit` therefore produces an unsigned commit silently (no error) unless explicitly checked with `git log --show-signature`. Prior commits already on this branch (e.g. 7d3dfda) DO carry real signatures, but from a GitHub RSA key (git log --show-signature shows 'Signature made ... using RSA key', not an SSH signature) -- consistent with those commits having been created via the GitHub API (push_files/PR-merge web-flow autosigning), not via a local `git commit` in a sandbox like this one.
evidence: `ssh-add -l | ...` -> `/bin/bash: line 2: ssh-add: command not found` in this session's container

`git config --get gpg.format` -> `ssh`; `git config --get user.signingkey` -> `/home/claude/.ssh/commit_signing_key.pub`; that file exists but `wc -c` reports 0 bytes; no private key file found anywhere under /home/claude/.ssh/
A local `git commit` in this session produced a commit with `git log -1 --show-signature` reporting `No signature`, despite `commit.gpgsign=true`

`git log -1 --show-signature 7d3dfda` (a commit already on this branch, from an earlier session) reports `Signature made ... using RSA key B5690EEEBB952194` -- a GPG RSA signature, not an SSH one, despite the repo's gpg.format=ssh config -- strongly consistent with GitHub's own web-flow/API autosigning rather than a local signing setup
fieldValues.body: srs#729's PR (https://github.com/the-greenman/srs/pull/770) was pushed with an unsigned local commit after this was discovered, disclosed transparently in the PR body, and NOT worked around by fabricating a signature or disabling verification. Branch protection on this repo requires validate-all + check-release-drift as status checks (per CLAUDE.md), not commit signatures, so the push was not blocked. This is a tool/environment gap, not a data or process gap: either (a) CLAUDE.md's signing section should be scoped explicitly to local-CLI sessions only (it already says '(local CLI use)' in its heading, but the instruction as written gives no fallback for a cloud/remote session where the check can never pass), or (b) the remote sandbox image should provision a working signing key so cloud-agent commits can be verified the same way a human's local commits are. Filing as a finding rather than silently choosing (a) or (b) myself, since it's an infrastructure/process decision, not a spec decision this unit's Door 3 scope covers.
